correctness.independent_verification: The complete nonstandard step is the two-way matching/leaf-filler equivalence; the source proof was reconstructed rather than inferred from its regression check. Distinctions from immediate-successor morphisms, root-fixed embeddings, leaf-fixed embeddings, infinite trees and frames with valuations are essential.
correctness.rationale: Write T_x for the whole descendant cone in the reflexive ancestor frame. The bounded-morphism condition is exactly f(T_x)=U_{f(x)} for each x. At a source s mapping to t, either a source child cone also maps onto U_t (case A), or the children of t can be injected into distinct children of s whose cones map onto each corresponding U_d (case B). Necessity uses the forward condition and immediate covering, and the unused cones in the converse can map constantly to an actual leaf of U_t; such constants are p-morphisms because the leaf cone is singleton. An injective target-to-source strict-ancestry/LCA embedding has exactly the same A/B recurrence, permitting e(target root) below source root and not constraining source leaves. Source-size induction, including leaf t and unary s, therefore proves equivalence. At root, surjectivity follows. Bipartite child matching yields polynomial time. Independent brute force of 196 source/target shape pairs <=5 nodes compared literal all-function p-morphism tests against literal injective ancestry/LCA embeddings. These finite checks do not establish the all-finite-tree theorem alone.
